## Introduction

For this assignment, I am using The Wonderful Wizard of Oz by L. Frank Baum. I wanted to use a fantasy novel and see how its words can be organized into a tidy dataframe. I will follow the workflow from Chapter 1 of Text Mining with R.

## 1. Import Text

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(tidytext)
library(gutenbergr)

dir.create("data", showWarnings = FALSE)

if (!file.exists("data/oz.csv")) {
  oz_download <- gutenberg_download(55)
  write_csv(oz_download, "data/oz.csv")
}

oz <- read_csv("data/oz.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  mutate(line = row_number())

oz
```


## 2. Make the Text Tidy

```{r}
tidy_oz <- oz |>
  unnest_tokens(word, text)

tidy_oz
```


## 3. Count Words

```{r}
word_counts <- tidy_oz |>
  count(word, sort = TRUE)

head(word_counts, 10)
```


## 4. Remove Stop Words

```{r}
oz_words <- tidy_oz |>
  anti_join(stop_words, by = "word")

word_counts2 <- oz_words |>
  count(word, sort = TRUE)

head(word_counts2, 10)
```


## 5. Plot the Most Common Words

```{r}
word_counts2 |>
  slice_max(n, n = 10, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(word, n), y = n)) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    title = "Most Common Words in The Wonderful Wizard of Oz",
    x = "Word",
    y = "Number of Times Used"
  )
```
